legend: Poikiloderma. Extensor surface of lower leg demonstrating the chronic phase with skin atrophy, marbleized mixed hypopigmentation, and hyperpigmentation with telangiectasia.
Radial ray defect manifest as missing thumb.

diagnosis: Rothmund–Thomson syndrome, Baller–Gerold syndrome, and RAPADILINO syndrome (associated with RECQL4 pathogenic variants) and their overlapping clinical features

legend: Histopathological features of poikiloderma characteristically seen in Rothmund–Thomson syndrome, with prominent superficial dermal vessels, minimal basal cell vacuolization, and intraepidermal dyskeratotic cells.
Osteoblastic osteosarcoma, the most common malignancy seen in Rothmund–Thomson syndrome, displays pleomorphic osteoblasts and eosinophilic malignant osteoid.
